---
title: "Charts"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110)
```

```{r}
library(phwstyle)
library(ggplot2)
use_phw_ggplot()
set.seed(1)
cases <- data.frame(
  onset = as.Date("2025-01-06") + round(rgamma(400, 5, 0.12)),
  age_group = sample(c("0-14", "15-44", "45-64", "65+"), 400, TRUE),
  sex = sample(c("Female", "Male"), 400, TRUE),
  setting = sample(c("Setting 1", "Setting 2", "Setting 3"), 400, TRUE, prob = c(0.6, 0.15, 0.25)),
  organism = sample(c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 400, TRUE)
)
```

`use_phw_ggplot()` sets `theme_phw()` and the PHW colour scales for every
plot in the session, and styles extension geoms. Everything below is plain
ggplot2.

## Colours that stay with their groups

A colour key fixes each level's colour. Use the same `key` in every chart
(and in `phw_reactable()`, `phw_leaflet_polygons()` or
`phw_flextable_groups()`) and "Setting 2" is always the same colour.

```{r}
ggplot(cases, aes(age_group, fill = setting)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_phw_d(key = "setting") +
  labs(title = "Cases by age group and setting", x = NULL, y = "Cases",
       caption = phw_caption("Example data"))
```

## Shapes and line types as a second cue

```{r}
weekly <- as.data.frame(table(week = cut(cases$onset, "week"), organism = cases$organism))
weekly$week <- as.Date(weekly$week)
ggplot(weekly, aes(week, Freq, colour = organism, shape = organism)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_phw_d(palette = "accessible") + scale_shape_phw() +
  labs(title = "Weekly cases by type", x = NULL, y = "Cases")
```

## Public health charts

```{r}
phw_epicurve(cases, "onset", group = "organism") +
  labs(title = "Cases by week of onset", x = "Week beginning", y = "Cases")
```

```{r}
phw_pyramid(cases, "age_group", "sex", percent = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Cases by age and sex")
```

```{r}
units <- data.frame(area = paste("Area", 1:30), eligible = round(runif(30, 300, 6000)))
units$events <- rbinom(30, units$eligible, c(rep(0.72, 28), 0.6, 0.82))
phw_funnel(units, "events", "eligible", label = "area") +
  labs(title = "Proportion by area", x = "Population", y = "Proportion (%)")
```

```{r}
monthly <- data.frame(month = seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 30),
                      value = c(rnorm(20, 50, 4), rnorm(10, 57, 4)))
phw_spc(monthly, "month", "value", improvement = "increase", baseline = 20) +
  labs(title = "Monthly measure")
```

## Finishing and saving

`phw_finalise()` adds the logo, source and date under a chart (or a
patchwork, or any grob), and `phw_save()` saves it with the bundled font.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
p <- phw_epicurve(cases, "onset") + labs(title = "Cases by week")
phw_save(phw_finalise(p, source = "Example data", date = Sys.Date()), "epicurve.png")
```

## Several charts in one figure

```{r, fig.width = 10, eval = requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)}
a <- ggplot(cases, aes(y = setting)) + geom_bar() + labs(x = "Cases", y = NULL)
b <- phw_epicurve(cases, "onset", interval = "month") + labs(y = "Cases")
phw_arrange(a, b, widths = c(1, 2), title = "Two charts, one title", source = "Example data",
            tag_levels = "A")
```
